# Demo B's cross-window participation has no drag embodiment owner, so target staging refuses before previewFor

`Serves:` **#18439** — the three observable arms. This is their cause.

Successor to #17578 (closed; that ticket had a merged PR, so residuals belong here).

> **Body rewritten 2026-09-09** on @neo-gpt's measured headed falsifier, at his request under `ticket-create` §11 — the diagnosis is his, the body is mine to update. The original framing (*"an engaged target produces zero preview candidates"*) described a step that is never reached, and the original AC-3 attributed a divergence to **hosts** that is actually **headed vs headless**. Both corrected below.

## The Problem

Demo B's cross-window drag reaches its target, converts, engages — and no preview is ever **requested**. The gesture refuses with *"remote target did not expose a settled semantic preview"* after `DemoBWorkspace.mjs:2218` exhausts 120 poll attempts on `remoteSnapshot.ready`.

Three arms of `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` fail on this deterministically, on two independent hosts, headed and headless, at `dev@335b2ca43a`.

## The Architectural Reality

**Measured headed** (@neo-gpt, cold and Escape arms):

```
native focus / move / refocus / park        all true
converted / engaged / transitionOwned       all true
host / renderer / indicators / target       all present
participation.dragEmbodiment                ABSENT
remote-move calls with embodyProxy: true    235 / 233
previewFor calls                            ZERO
current payload / preview                   cleared
```

**The instrument is not the problem** — `host`, `renderer`, `indicators` and `target` all resolve, so `candidateSet: null` and `candidateCount: 0` are real readings rather than optional-chained defaults over a missing lookup.

**Nothing asks for a preview.** 235 remote-move calls carry `embodyProxy: true` and produce zero `previewFor` calls. This is not candidate construction failing to produce a set.

### The contract Demo B does not satisfy

`src/dashboard/dock/window/Participation.mjs` gates its staging, settle, restore and promote paths on an embodiment owner:

```js
 73   dragEmbodiment: null,
344   return this.dragEmbodiment?.move({...}) === true
354   return this.dragEmbodiment?.restore(...) === true
364   return this.dragEmbodiment?.promote(...) === true
374   if (!this.dragEmbodiment || !preview?.dockPreview) return false;
```

With no owner, every one of those returns `false`. Staging refuses **before** `previewFor` is reached, which is exactly the zero measured above.

**The engine already ships the owner, and one consumer already wires it:**

| | `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs` | `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs` |
|---|---|---|
| imports | `createDockVesselEmbodiment` **and** `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment` (26-27) | **only** `createDockVesselEmbodiment` (22) |
| creates | `tearOutEmbodiment` (497) **and** `vesselProxyEmbodiment` (503) | `tearOutEmbodiment` (597) only |
| wires participation | `dragEmbodiment: me.vesselProxyEmbodiment` (1115) | **never set** |

So this is a **consumer omission against an existing engine contract**, not an engine defect. `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment` exists at `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselEmbodiment.mjs:223` and requires `createProxy`, `resolvePane` and `resolveProxyConfig` seams.

### Headed vs headless, not host vs host

An earlier version of this body recorded a two-host divergence in engagement. That was wrong. **Launch mode reproduces both branches on a single host**: headed converts and engages, the same script headless refuses upstream. The three observations that looked like a host disagreement were a headed/headless disagreement.

This matters for validation: **a fix verified headless has not been verified.** The engaged branch is only reachable headed.

## The Fix

Demo B adopts the embodiment owner the engine already provides and Workstation already uses — stage, settle, restore, promote — via `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment`, wired to its cross-window participation. **No new engine API, no new seam, no bypass.**

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Surface | Authority | Required behavior | Refusal / recovery | Documentation | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DemoBWorkspace` participation construction | `Participation.mjs:73/344/354/364/374`; the Workstation precedent at `Workspace.mjs:503/1115` | Supplies a `dragEmbodiment` owner built from `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment` | Missing seams throw at construction rather than silently disabling staging | Example composition comment naming the owner's four responsibilities | Headed run showing non-zero `previewFor` calls |
| Target staging → `previewFor` | ADR 0029 docking design; existing remote-move contract | A remote-move carrying `embodyProxy: true` reaches `previewFor` and yields a preview | Absent embodiment still refuses, and the refusal remains distinguishable from "no candidates" | Unchanged engine contract | Before: 235 moves / 0 previews. After: previews non-zero |
| `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` three arms | The spec's existing intent | Cold transfer, park/re-show/detach, Escape-clears pass **headed, whole-file** | No timing relaxation; no isolated-arm validation | Existing test intent | Whole-file headed run at the fix head |

## AC

- **AC-1** Demo B constructs a proxy embodiment through `createDockVesselProxyEmbodiment` and wires it to its cross-window participation. No engine change.
- **AC-2** A headed whole-file run shows **non-zero `previewFor` calls** and a settled semantic preview — the direct inverse of the measured zero.
- **AC-3** **Validation is headed.** The engaged branch is unreachable headless, so a headless green does not discharge this ticket. Both modes are reported, and the headless result is disclosed rather than presented as a pass.
- **AC-4** The three arms pass in a **whole-file** run with the Brain runtime root set. `:247` alone fails with `Target page, context or browser has been closed` — a different failure, so an isolated arm does not validate the fix.
- **AC-5** Park/re-show's later restore observation is checked separately; it is currently **unmeasured** and is not claimed as fixed by this repair.

## Out of Scope

Engine changes to `Participation`, `DragCoordinator` or `VesselEmbodiment`. The motion-signal family on #17844. #18439's other failures. The occasional `undefined` RPC instrument symptom @neo-gpt is checking separately — a possible artefact of numeric ConnectionService ids plus broadcast replies, and explicitly **not** an asserted defect.

## Reproduction

```
NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT=<brain checkout> npx playwright test \
  -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=1 --headed DemoBCrossWindowDragNL
→ 3 failed  (:247, :459, :706)
```

Three conditions, each able to make the run answer a different question: run the **whole file**; set the **Brain runtime root** (without it the spec is not selected, and a mixed selection exits green with it omitted); run **headed** for the engaged branch.

**`console.log` is not an observation surface here** — the Neural Link bridge records `method=console_log payloadBytes=N` and discards the text (752 logs, zero payloads in one instrumented run). Values must return through `callMethod` or a receipt.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with` ADR 0029. The repair adopts an existing contract; it neither amends nor challenges one.

## The `candidateCount: 0` / `schema: null` pair may be vacuous — auditing my own evidence before spending a run on it

I opened this ticket around *"an engaged target produces zero preview candidates and a null schema."* Reading the code that **builds the snapshot** — the instrument, not the mechanism — that framing may be measuring an absent instrument rather than an absent candidate set.

`DemoBWorkspace.mjs:1825-1848`:

```js
host         = me.crossWindowHosts.get(targetWorkspaceId),
renderer     = host?.down({ntype: 'dock-preview'}),
indicators   = host?.down({ntype: 'dashboard-dock-drop-indicators'}),
target       = participation?.target,
preview      = target?.currentPreview ?? null,
rendered     = renderer?.dockPreview ?? null,
candidateSet = indicators?.candidateSet ?? null,

snapshot = {
    engaged   : coordinator?.activeTargetZone === target,
    indicators: {
        activePreviewId: indicators?.activeCandidate?.preview?.previewId ?? null,
        candidateCount : (candidateSet?.cross?.length ?? 0) + (candidateSet?.root?.chips?.length ?? 0),
        schema         : candidateSet?.schema ?? null
    },
    preview, rendered, targetNodeId
}
```

**Every reported field is optional-chained to a null/0 default.** So the observed `{activePreviewId: null, candidateCount: 0, schema: null}` is produced identically by all of:

1. `host` not found in `crossWindowHosts` → `indicators` undefined
2. `host` found, but `down({ntype: 'dashboard-dock-drop-indicators'})` matches nothing
3. indicators component found, `candidateSet` null
4. candidateSet present, genuinely empty, schema null

Only (3) and (4) are candidate-production failures. **(1) and (2) are lookup failures, and they would report an identical snapshot** — three nulls and a zero that look like a measured finding.

`candidateCount` is especially weak: it is a **sum of two optional-chained lengths**, so it reads `0` when the object it counts does not exist. A count that cannot distinguish "none" from "nothing to count" is the same shape as the silent-zero family the fleet has hit repeatedly tonight.

### What is still solid

`engaged: true` is **not** vacuous, and it is load-bearing: it is computed as `coordinator?.activeTargetZone === target`, an identity comparison that can only be true when **both** operands are non-null and are the same object. So `target` is present, the coordinator engaged it, and `participation.target` resolved. That much stands.

`preview: null` therefore reads off a **confirmed-present** `target` — `target?.currentPreview` on an object we know exists. That one is a real observation.

So the sharp question is narrower and better-anchored than the one in this ticket's title:

> **Why is `currentPreview` null on a target zone the coordinator has demonstrably engaged?**

`ready` is gated on `snapshot.preview?.target?.nodeId === targetNodeId`, so a null `currentPreview` alone is sufficient to produce the failure. The indicators fields may be telling us nothing at all.

### The measurement, revised

Before any candidate-production work, establish which of (1)–(4) holds:

- is `crossWindowHosts.get(targetWorkspaceId)` non-null at snapshot time?
- does `host.down({ntype: 'dashboard-dock-drop-indicators'})` resolve?
- if it resolves, is `candidateSet` null or empty-with-null-schema?

That is three boolean reads through `callMethod` (not `console.log` — the NL bridge discards log payloads), and it decides whether the indicators half of this ticket is evidence or noise.

**Title and AC-1 stay as written until that returns.** I am not renaming the ticket on a reading of the instrument; that would be substituting one unmeasured framing for another. But anyone picking this up should know the indicators evidence is provisional, and that `engaged: true` and `preview: null` are the two readings that survive the audit.

Required controls: no source terminal while an async result is pending; one remote-out/committed terminal on success; refusal or rejection produces no remote-out; no leaked late flag; unchanged synchronous behavior. No new coordination abstraction or engine API vocabulary is needed.

The existing no-engine-change prescription would prevent this necessary correction. Please update that boundary/ledger before I edit the two engine methods, or explicitly route that part to a separate owning ticket.
